title: Outlook: Copilot insights on selected email text in classic Outlook for Windows
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates what Microsoft has said about data access, processing boundaries and execution identity. The rollout facts and control paths are supported, but Microsoft describes processing selected email content without saying that it is the only content processed or that no new permissions are involved.

claims.claim: Classic Outlook for Windows users can select email text and ask Copilot for contextual insights.
claims.quote: We're introducing User Initiated Insights in Copilot for classic Outlook for Windows, enabling users to manually select text within an email and prompt Copilot to provide contextual insights.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users control invocation of this feature by selecting email text and asking Copilot for insights.
claims.quote: Users control invocation by choosing when to select text and engage Copilot.

claims.claim: Copilot processes user-selected email content to generate insights.
claims.quote: The feature enables Copilot to process user-selected email content to generate insights.

claims.claim: Copilot processes only the text the user chooses to select.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook user initiated Copilot insights selected email content only context signed-in user permissions'. Read MC1311978, Copilot overview and privacy page; none states an exclusive selected-text processing boundary for Explain This.
claims.fix: Replace 'Copilot only processes text the user chooses to select' with 'Copilot processes user-selected email content to generate insights'. In Why it matters, replace 'Nothing reaches Copilot unless a user selects it and asks' with 'Users invoke this feature by selecting email text and asking Copilot for insights'.

claims.claim: This feature introduces no new access to data.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook user initiated Copilot insights selected email content only context signed-in user permissions'. Read MC1311978 and Copilot privacy page; continuing security policies do not establish that this feature introduces no new data access.
claims.fix: Replace 'This is a new way into Copilot, not new access' with 'This is a new way to invoke Copilot from selected email text'.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new data source for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook insights selected text Copilot' and 'Explain This Outlook Copilot'. Read MC1311978 and the roadmap description in full; both describe selecting email text, without identifying another data source.

claims.claim: The feature runs for the signed-in user inside Outlook.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook user initiated Copilot insights selected email content only context signed-in user permissions'. Read MC1311978, overview and privacy page; general user-permission boundaries do not document this feature's execution identity.
claims.fix: Replace 'the feature runs for the signed-in user inside Outlook' with 'the feature is built into the Outlook experience'.

claims.claim: No new permission is involved in this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook Explain This turn off Copilot permissions no new permissions' and 'user initiated insights Outlook disable permission'. Read MC1311978 and Copilot privacy page; no passage states that no new permission is involved.
claims.fix: Remove 'or permission' from 'no new add-in or permission is involved'; retain only the supported statement that no separate add-in is required.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe this feature acting on the mailbox.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook insights selected text Copilot' and 'Explain This Outlook Copilot'. Read the roadmap and MC1311978 in full; they describe generating insights, not mailbox modification or autonomous mailbox actions.

claims.claim: The app-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
Select the Available Apps list.
Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane.
Select Block app.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for blocking the built-in Copilot app through Integrated Apps is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph block Copilot app Integrated Apps API copilotPackage'. Read Package Management API overview and block reference excerpt; these cover agent/tool packages, not the built-in Copilot app. Read Integrated Apps guidance.

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat says the Integrated Apps block covers Copilot in Outlook, the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams and the web, including licensed users.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.fix: Keep the cited scope, but add: 'The Integrated Apps management page says its changes affect Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application, while Teams continues to honour Teams admin center settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365 for this conflicting scope.

claims.claim: The documented Integrated Apps controls require a Global Administrator.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.
